description_en: The temple stands within the lane that emerges from Yangaḥhiti in the Cikamugaḥ quarter. This lane is locally known as Mañjuśrī Galli (or MañjuśrīTole) after the temple itself. Facing west, the shrine preserves its original carved wooden doorway from the early construction phase, flanked on both sides by a pair of stone lions. Of theṭuṇḍalastruts supporting the temple, twelve belong to the original period, while others—stolen in the past—have been replaced with newer replicas. Both tiers of the temple roof are now sheeted with metal plates, and a gilded finial rises from the uppermost section. Inside thegarbhagṛhaare stone images and other archaeological objects collected over time.The principal icon enshrined here is an exceptionally rare image of Mañjuśrī in his childhood form, which is also worshipped locally as Sarasvatī. Sculptures depicting Mañjuśrī as a child are uncommon, and this particular example—dated stylistically to around the 10th century—therefore holds special significance. The pedestal bears an inscription whose date has eroded, but on palaeographic grounds, Regmi (1966, p. 2) assigns it to the 10th century. The inscription refers to the deity as Mañjunātha. The attachment of the -nāthasuffix to the bodhisattva’s name by this period suggests that the idea of Mañjunātha had already emerged within the Mahāyāna tradition, making the image important from a religious-historical perspective.The sculpture portrays Mañjuśrī with a small, childlike figure. In his right hand he appears to hold a fruit, while the object in his left hand is difficult to identify due to damage. The image has been cut open at the back, presumably to hollow it, and the plainparvāḥbehind the figure rises high with a raised central ridge. The combination of these features marks the sculpture as a significant work of early medieval art. The image was stolen in the later years of the Panchayat era but was fortunately recovered; after its return, the local community organized a grandjātrāto reinstall it. The rear portion of theparvāḥhad been broken during the theft. A pre-theft photograph clearly showing the intact image was published by Slusser and Vajrācārya (2005, p. 110, Fig. 3).Given the 10th-century date of the inscribed image, it is likely that a shrine of some form stood here during that time. The present structure, however, appears—based on its style and surviving wooden components—to belong to the late Malla period. This suggests that the old image was preserved in the sanctum when a new temple was constructed during the early modern period. The roofing of the upper tier with metal plates and the installation of a gilded finial took place during the reign of King Surendra, in NS 988 (1868 CE). Earlier, the lower roof was covered with traditionaljhiṅgaṭītiles, as seen in a photograph published by Pruscha (1975). During the reconstruction undertaken in VS 2040 (1983–84 CE) through local and organizational initiative, the lower roof was also sheeted with metal. The most recent restoration occurred in VS 2074 (2018 CE) under the oversight of the then-Member of Parliament Dhyāngovinda Rañjita, the Department of Archaeology, other stakeholders, and the local community.The temple formerly received daily worship from thegurujulineage of Tvāke Bāhāḥ, although regular rituals have since lapsed. Today, the Buddhist community of Kathmandu—especially followers of the Tibetan lineage of Guru Mañjuśrī Māni—performs special worship here onŚrīpañcamī, when the shrine attracts large crowds. Local residents also revere the deity as Sarasvatī, and on this occasion they bring young children to write their first letters as a symbolic initiation into learning.
description_ne: यस मन्दिरभित्र मञ्जुश्रीको बालावस्थाको निकै दुर्लभ पूर्वमध्यकालीन मूर्ति छ जसलाई सरस्वतीका रूपमा पनि पूजिँदै आएको छ ।चिकंमुगः टोलबाट यंगाःहिति निस्कने गल्लीमाँझ यो मन्दिर अवस्थित छ । यो गल्लीलाई यसै मन्दिरको नामबाट मञ्जुश्री गल्ली (टोल) भन्ने गरिन्छ । पश्चिमतिर फर्केको मन्दिरमा प्रारम्भिक निर्माणताकाको बुट्टेदार काँठको ढोका छ । ढोकाको दायाँबायाँ एकजोडा शिलाका सिंह प्रतिमा छन् । मन्दिरलाई थामेका टुँडालमध्ये १२ वटा प्रारम्भिक निर्माणकालका हुन् भने अन्य चोरी भई नयाँप्रति हालिएका छन् । मन्दिरका दुबै तहका छानामा हाल धातुको पाता मोडिएको छ र उचो भागमा सुवर्ण गजुर चढाइएको छ । मन्दिरको गर्भगृहमा विविध शिलाका मूर्ति एवं अन्य पुरातात्विक सामग्री संग्रहित छन् । मन्दिरमा मुख्य मूर्तिका रूपमा स्थापित मञ्जुश्रीको बालावस्थाको मूर्ति निकै विशेष छ । कारण, मञ्जुश्रीको बालक स्वरूप देखाइएको मूर्ति निकै दुर्लभ छ । करिब १० औं शदीमा बनेको मूर्ति भएबाट पनि यसको महत्व बढेको छ । यस मूर्तिको पादमा अभिलेख छ । मिति खिइसकेको यस अभिलेखलाई लिपिका आधारमा Regmi (1966, p. 2) ले १० औं शदीतिरको थानेका छन् । अभिलेखमा यस मूर्तिलाई मञ्जुनाथ भनिएको छ । महायानी सम्प्रदायका मञ्जुश्रीमा ‘नाथ’ प्रत्यय जोडी सो समयमै ‘मञ्जुनाथ’ को अवधारणा विकास भैसक्नु धार्मिक दृष्टिले पनि निकै रोचक देखिन्छ । मूर्तिमा मञ्जुश्रीको कद सानो छ र बालक अवस्थाको मुखाकृति देखिन्छ । उनले दायाँ हातले कुनै फल र बायाँबाट केही वस्तु लिएको देखा पर्छ तर बायाँ हातले समाएको वस्तु निश्चय गर्न कठिन छ । मूर्तिको अनावश्यक भाग काटी वायुदार बनाइएको छ । मूर्ति पछाडिको सादा पर्वाःको उचो भागमा चोसो उठाइएको छ । यसरी मूर्तिकलाका दृष्टिले पनि यो मूर्ति निकै खास छ । अनेक दृष्टिले महत्व बोकेको यस मूर्ति पञ्चायतकालको उत्तरार्धमा चोरी भएको थियो । चोरी भैसकेको मूर्ति भाग्यवस् फेला परी स्थानीयले भव्य जात्रा गरी पुनर्स्थापना गरेका थिए । चोरीका क्रममा मूर्ति पछाडिको पर्वाः खण्डित भएको थियो । चोरी पूर्वको सम्पूर्ण भाग स्पष्ट देखा पर्ने यस मूर्तिको फोटो Slusser & Vajracharya (2005, प। 110/Fig 3) ले प्रकाशमा ल्याएकी छन् ।१० औं शदीतिरको मानिएको अभिलेख सहितको मूर्ति भएबाट यहाँ सोही समयमा कुनै आकारको मन्दिर बनेको हुनु पर्दछ । हाल उभिएको मन्दिरको शैली र प्राप्त काष्ठसामग्री नियाल्दा उत्तरमल्लकालीन देखिन्छ । यसर्थ पुरानो मूर्तिलाई गर्भगृहमा राखी उत्तरमध्यकालमा नयाँ मन्दिर निर्माण भएको देखिन्छ । मन्दिरको माथिल्लो छानोलाई सुवर्ण गजूर सहित पाताले मोड्ने कार्य राजा सुरेन्द्रको शासनकाल अर्थात् नेसं ९८८ (सन् १८६८) मा भएको थियो । मन्दिरको तल्लो छानो झिंगटीको हुने गर्दथ्यो जुन Pruscha (1975, p. ) द्वारा प्रकाशित फोटोमा देख्न सकिन्छ । विसं २०४० (सन् १९८३-३४) सालमा स्थानीय र सरोकालवाला संस्थाको सक्रियतामा  मन्दिरको पुनर्निर्माण गरिँदा तल्लो छानो पनि पाताले नै मोडिएको थियो । मन्दिरको पछिल्लो जीर्णोद्धार विसं २०७४ (सन् २०१८) मा तत्कालीन सांसद् ध्यानगोविन्द रञ्जित, पुरातत्त्व विभाग एवं अन्य सरोकालवाला सहित स्थानीयको रोहवरमा भएको थियो ।यस मन्दिरमा त्वाके बाहाःका गुरुजु खलकबाट नित्य पूजा हुँदै आएको थियो । हाल यहाँ नित्य पूजा हुन छाडेको छ । मन्दिरको मूर्तिलाई काठमाडौंका बौद्ध समुदायले तिब्बतबाट आएका गुरु मञ्जुश्री मानी विशेषतः श्रीपञ्चमीका दिन पूजा गर्ने गर्छन् । यस दिन मन्दिरमा मेला जस्तै भीड लाग्ने गर्दछ । स्थानीयले सरस्वतीका रूपमा पनि पुजी साना बालबालिकालाई विद्या आरम्भको संकेतमा अक्षेर लेखाउन ल्याउने थिति छ ।

historical_events.event_description: The inscription on the base of the main deity of the temple records that the image of Mañjunātha was installed. Although the date on the inscription is eroded, Regmi (1966, p. 2) has dated it to around 10th century.
Bhājumāṃ and other family members jointly offered a bell in the name of Mañjeśvarī (Mañjuśrī).

A partially damaged stone oil lamp is kept within the sanctum. An inscription is engraved on its surface, though nearly half of it has weathered away. The stand bears carved figures of the donor family, with their names inscribed in the lower  part of the images. The donors of this object were Ganasiṃ and Cikuti. It remains uncertain whether the oil lamp stand was originally dedicated to this temple or brought here from elsewhere, where it might have been simply lying around.

The temple is flanked by a pair of stone lion statues. An inscription carved on the lower part (pedestal) of the statues records that they were installed in front of the temple by Bisamā and twelve other individuals.

During the reign of King Surendra, the temple’s previous tile roof was replaced with gilt copper sheets. Similar gilt eave boards, inscribed with embossed letters, were also installed on all sides of the upper roof.

In the northwestern corner of the temple is a small courtyard containing two caitya and a historic well. One of the caitya bears an inscription on the lower part of its eastern surface. According to the inscription, a Persian resident of the same courtyard, named Kehemāna, along with his family members, constructed this caitya.

Bhājumāna Ranjitakāra, along with his family members who resided near the temple, installed a brass banner inside the sanctum. The walls of the temple’s ground floor were decorated with imported tiles. Furthermore, they also installed sixty oil lamps surrounding the temple.
In VS 2040 (1983–84), the temple was jointly rebuilt by all concerned bodies. Local residents, the elected ward committee, and the priestly clan collectively contributed to its reconstruction.
Following the theft of the original image in the 1980s, Guṇanidhi Rañjita undertook the reinstallation of a replacement statue of Durgā on the left pedestal.

The restoration work of the temple was carried out in the presence of the then Member of Parliament Dhyan Govinda Ranjit, representatives from the Department of Archaeology, other concerned authorities, and local residents.
